Some residents of Enugu have urged government at all levels in the state to provide food storage facilities in localities to reduce post-harvest losses of onions.
The residents, who spoke to the News Agency of Nigeria on Friday in Enugu in separate interviews, said that lack of storage facilities had led to scarcity and an increase in the produce’s price.
A resident of Achara Layout, Paul Igwe, said that onion farmers in Nigeria lose so much money annually due to post-harvest losses.
“Every year, onion farmers lose a lot of produce which would have yielded sufficient money for them due to a lack of facilities for storage,” he said.
An onion seller at Garki Market, Gloria Kalu, said onion is now “gold” due to its scarcity and price hike.
According to Mrs Kalu, storage facilities for various types of foodstuffs are essential because they will curb food scarcity, which usually leads to an increase in the price of farm produce.
A civil servant, Chidi Uzor, said that providing food storage facilities and constructing a standard road network linking farms and markets would also eliminate post-harvest loss.

Another onion seller at new Garki Market, Gambo Haruna, said the price of onions increases daily due to the off-season period and non-availability of storage facilities.
According to Mr Haruna, a bag of onions now sells for ₦400,000, up from ₦250,000 in October.
Joy Okoroafor, another onion seller at Mayor Market, said one medium-sized onion now sells for ₦500, compared to ₦200 in October.
A farmer, Chijioke James, said that tackling post-harvest food losses should be declared as an emergency in the country.
Mr James noted that insecurity, low yield per hectare seedlings, and outdated agro-inputs, methods and implements are already fueling acute food shortage.
Meanwhile, Kenneth Eze, chairman of the Enugu Young Farmers Association, said onions could be cultivated year-round, adding that people are unaware of the latest planting technique.
“If people are trained on modern farm techniques and year-round planting seasons, onions will not be scarce again,” Mr Eze said.
He said providing food storage facilities would also go a long way toward preventing onion scarcity.
